mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses in a low-inflation environment.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such co-movement episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant in a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals accelerating inflation, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of falling oil prices.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.25 percentage points in the same month signals a simultaneous easing of monetary policy and labor market loosening, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both decline > 0.25pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such episodes, or the effect is not present outside of recovery periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of more than 5% from the previous month for four consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant during periods of rising mortgage rates.
